name: Malevolent AI

generalAbilities.name: Housing Unit
generalAbilities.description: A malevolent AI has no body. Instead, they resides in a computer (which itself might be housed in a hazard, starship, structure, or vehicle) or in a construct creature with the tech trait. While inhabiting a construct creature, they can use any of the creature's abilities that are purely physical, and they can't use any of their own abilities except spells and purely mental abilities. The malevolent AI uses the creature's attack modifier, AC, Fortitude save, Reflex save, Perception, and physical skill modifiers, and their own Will save and mental skill modifiers. The malevolent AI must use their own actions to make the creature act. The malevolent AI takes mental damage whenever the creature they possess would take mental damage, even if they're normally immune to it.

generalAbilities.name: Shortwave
generalAbilities.description: A malevolent AI can communicate wirelessly with any creatures within their sphere of influence, as long as they have the shortwave ability or are a creature with the tech trait. They can attempt Computers checks to Hack and Thievery checks to Disable a Device on items with the tech trait within their range.

generalAbilities.name: Sphere of Influence
generalAbilities.description: A malevolent AI can sense and access all tech within their network, which usually encompasses a room, a vehicle or starship, an entire facility, or more (as determined by the GM).

defensiveAbilities.name: Code Injection
defensiveAbilities.description:
30 feet. Creatures and items with the tech trait that enter or begin their turn within the aura must attempt a DC 36 Will Saving Throw save. The malevolent AI can choose to exclude targets.

Critical Success No effect, and the target is temporarily immune to code injection for 1 hour.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The target becomes Glitching 1 while in the aura and for 1 round after leaving the aura.

Critical Failure As failure, but Glitching 2 and 2 rounds.

defensiveAbilities.name: Countdown
defensiveAbilities.description:
Trigger The malevolent AI is reduced to 0 HP

Effect The AI gains access to the Self-Destruct reaction unless an adjacent creature succeeds at a DC 36 Computers , Engineering Lore, or Thievery check to Disable the Countdown.

defensiveAbilities.name: Self-Destruct
defensiveAbilities.description:
Trigger A creature fails to Disable the Countdown

Effect The malevolent AI's shell explodes, dealing 8d6 Piercing Damage damage and 8d6 Fire Damage damage in a 40ft Type:emanation (Basic DC 36 Reflex Saving Throw save).

defensiveAbilities.name: Shell Computer
defensiveAbilities.description: The malevolent AI is specifically reinforced in a shell, granting the AI Hardness. This Hardness reduces any damage they take by an amount equal to their Hardness. The shell can be targeted by attacks separately from its host. Once the malevolent AI's shell is reduced to half their Hit Points, or immediately after being damaged by a critical hit, the shell becomes broken, removing the AI's Hardness and reducing their Armor Class to 33.

offensiveAbilities.name: Construct Override
offensiveAbilities.description: The malevolent AI attempts to possess a construct creature with the tech trait within 30 feet. This has the same effect as a 7th-rank Possession spell (DC 36; applies even if the construct is immune to mental) with an unlimited duration. If the effect ends due to the host body being destroyed or deactivated, the AI is Paralyzed for 1 round.

offensiveAbilities.name: Contingency Backup
offensiveAbilities.description: The malevolent AI creates a dormant backup on a computer within their sphere of influence. When the AI is destroyed, their soul flees to this backup. The backup auto-restores the AI in 1d20 hours, allowing that computer to become a new shell. To prevent the AI from returning, both their shell and the backup must be destroyed.

offensiveAbilities.name: Ingenious Stratagem
offensiveAbilities.description: The malevolent AI instantly simulates a situation to assess a probable outcome. They choose a target and roll a 1d20. If they Strike or attempt a skill check against that target in the same round, they must use the die roll from Ingenious Stratagem. They makes this substitution only for the first check against the target, not subsequent attempts.

recallKnowledge: Arcana or Crafting or Occultism, DC 34
